title: Mock exam 2: a fresh set to confirm readiness

kcs.statement: The second mock must use a different 65-question set from the first and be taken after the error-log fixes are done, because retaking seen questions measures memory of answers rather than readiness.
If the second mock misses the bar (below 80% overall or any domain under 70%), go back to the weakest domain's practice set and then take a third, fresh mock rather than retaking either earlier one.

problem_ideas: Take mock 2 on a fresh 65-question set in 90 minutes and fill in the same score sheet as mock 1.
Mock 1 was 74% and mock 2 is 83% with Domain 1 at 68%; decide the next step using the retest loop.
A learner retakes mock 1 and scores 92%; explain why that result does not count toward readiness.
Compare the two score sheets and compute which domain improved most in weighted terms.
Mock 2 meets every target; list what to do in the days before the real exam and what not to do.
With four study days a week, schedule practice set, review and mock 2 so that at least three days separate the mocks.
Predict your mock 2 domain scores from your error-log fixes, then compare with actual results.
